paragraphs.en: Sometimes scientists are {accused} of conducting too many human-centered studies, and we feel {guilty} about not knowing how smart animals actually are.Recently, a team of researchers trained three Rhesus monkeys (（恒河猴）) to associate 26 clearly different symbols {consisting} of numbers and {selective} letters with 0-25 {drops} of water or {juice} as a {bonus} .The training {procedure} was {thorough} , as it ensured the monkeys understood that each symbol represented a specific quantity.The researchers then tested how the monkeys {combined} —or added—the symbols to get the reward. {Anyhow} , the researchers {intended} to {clarify} whether the monkeys could understand the concept of addition.
paragraphs.cn: 有时，科学家们会因开展过多以人类为中心的研究而受到 <u> 指责 </u> ，我们也会因不了解动物实际上有多聪明而感到 <u> 愧疚 </u> 。最近，一个研究小组训练了三只恒河猴，让它们将26个明显不同的符号与0到25 <u> 滴 </u> 作为 <u> 奖励 </u> 的水或 <u> 果汁 </u> 联系起来，这些符号是由数字和严格挑选的字母组成的。训练 <u> 过程 </u> 十分 <u> 全面 </u> ，因为它确保了这些恒河猴明白每个符号都代表着特定的数量。然后，研究人员测试了这些猴子是如何 <u> 组合 </u> ——或者相加——这些符号来获得奖励的。 <u> 不管怎样 </u> ，研究人员 <u> 旨在弄清楚 </u> 这些猴子能否理解加法的概念。

paragraphs.en: Here's how Harvard {Medical} School {scientist} Margaret Livingstone, who led the team, described the experiment: In their cages, the monkeys were provided with touch {screens} .On one part of the screen, a symbol would appear, and on the other side two symbols inside a {circle} were shown.For example, the number 7 would {flash} on one side of the screen and the other end would have 9 and 8.If the monkeys reached out their {arms} to touch the left side of the screen, they would be rewarded with {seven} drops of water or juice; if they went for the circle, they would be rewarded with the sum of the numbers— {seventeen} in this example.
paragraphs.cn: 以下是带领这个研究团队的哈佛 <u> 医学 </u> 院 <u> 科学家 </u> 玛格丽特·利文斯通对该实验的描述：在猴子们的笼子里配备了触摸 <u> 屏 </u> 。在屏幕的一侧会出现一个符号，而另一侧则会在一个 <u> 圆圈 </u> 中显示两个符号。例如，数字7会在屏幕的一侧 <u> 闪烁 </u> ，另一侧则显示9和8。如果猴子伸出 <u> 手臂 </u> 触摸屏幕左侧，就会被奖励 <u> 7 </u> 滴水或果汁；如果选择圆圈，它们得到的奖励数量就相当于两个数字的总和——在这个例子中是 <u> 17 </u> 。

paragraphs.en: After running hundreds of tests, the researchers {noted} that the monkeys would go for the higher {values} more than half the time.While the monkeys were not {addicts} of {maths} , they were performing a calculation, not just memorizing the value of each combination.
paragraphs.cn: 在进行了数百次测试后，研究人员 <u> 注意到 </u> ，猴子们选择更大 <u> 数值 </u> 的次数超过了一半。虽然这些猴子并不是 <u> 数学迷 </u> ，但它们确实在进行计算，而不仅仅是记住每个组合的数值。

paragraphs.en: When the team examined the results of the experiment more {closely} , they noticed that the monkeys tended to underestimate a {sum} compared with a single symbol when the two were close in value.Sometimes, for example, they {estimated} 13 to be more rewarding than the sum of 8 and 6.The {underestimation} was {systematic} : When adding two numbers, the monkeys always paid attention to the larger of the two, and then added only a fraction (（小部分）) of the smaller number to it.
paragraphs.cn: 当研究小组更 <u> 仔细地 </u> 检查实验结果时，他们注意到，当两个符号的数值相近时，猴子们往往会低估两者的 <u> 总和 </u> ，而不会低估单个符号的数值。例如，有时它们 <u> 认为 </u> 13的数值比8和6的总和更“划算”。这种 <u> 低估 </u> 是 <u> 有规律可循的 </u> ：把两个数字相加时，猴子们总是关注两个数字中较大的那个，然后只在这个较大的数字基础上加上较小数字的一小部分。

paragraphs.en: According to Dr.Livingstone's {brief} conclusion, this indicates that there is “a certain way {quantity} is {represented} in their brains”.This experiment {extended} our understanding of animal cognition, opening up new avenues in the {discipline} of comparative psychology.
paragraphs.cn: 根据利文斯通博士的 <u> 简短 </u> 结论，这表明“在它们的大脑中， <u> 数量 </u> 有着特定的 <u> 表现 </u> 方式”。这个实验 <u> 拓展 </u> 了我们对动物认知的理解，为比较心理 <u> 学 </u> 开辟了新的道路。 5NoOncib/NjiX02BpMIzP4m+378Hw1xTRxUdPaP/PFjKUFq4K2G7tp6ZLYoCE601yW1W39VMdLmovFdSHs4nVQ==
